description:
Track all your AI coding subscription usage from the Windows system tray.

OpenTokenUsage is a lightweight system-tray app that tracks how much of your AI coding subscriptions you've used (Claude, Codex, Copilot, Cursor, Gemini, and more) in one place. It is a Windows fork of OpenUsage with full Windows support, a plugin-based provider system, and a local HTTP usage API.
Desktop widgets and a screen-edge rail, what you spend each day, six new providers, and a panel you can widen.
New Features
- Desktop widgets (Settings → Taskbar & desktop): the taskbar strip's providers anywhere on the desktop, side by side, stacked, one per provider or each in turn. Drag them where you like; they snap to screen edges and to each other, can stay on top, be locked in place or let clicks pass through to the window behind. A click opens the panel, the pointer shows when each limit resets, a number that goes up blinks, and they hide while a full-screen app is in front
- Screen-edge rail, a widget layout: today's tokens and spend, each provider's logo in a ring filled as far as its usage, and the live token rate, tucked against the right, left or top edge of the screen until the pointer comes near. It slides out smoothly (or jumps, as you choose), can take a soft color gradient, and has its own refresh button and a pin that keeps it open
- Taskbar strip: follow the active app (the AI tool in the window you're using goes first, in detail if you like), a dot on a logo while its agent works or waits for you, live tokens per minute for Claude and Codex (also in the tray's hover text), colors by pace, and an option to show the strip only while one of its providers' apps or CLIs runs. A new install starts with usage colors off; installs from before keep theirs
- Spend summary under the cards: today, yesterday and the last 30 days in tokens and API-price cost, the models you used most, and, with your subscription prices set, how many times its price each plan's use was worth. It reads the tools' own logs on this PC; tokscale can add about 30 more tools (off by default; it runs with bunx or npx)
- Claude and Codex cards show their live sessions, how full each one's context window is, and the time left on a Claude session's prompt cache. The detail pages add a year of daily use with streaks, and the weekly limit tells about how many tokens it holds at this week's mix of models
- Usage is kept after Claude Code deletes its logs (it does after 30 days by default), and Settings can change how long Claude Code keeps them. Daily tokens and the latest limits can be exported as CSV and JSON to Downloads, now or once a day
- Alerts when a limit refills before its reset (a reset credit or a partial refill)
- Cards: rearrange or hide their rows (drag, Ctrl+Z undoes), switch between what's used and what's left, and copy a card as an image
- New providers: Codebuff (credits and the weekly limit), Kilo (credit blocks and the Kilo Pass month), Kimi API (the platform balance, vouchers and cash), Ollama (installed and loaded models on this PC), Qwen Code (requests today and this month, from the CLI's own ledger) and Custom balances (up to five New API, One API or Sub2API accounts, or your own endpoint; the key stays in an environment variable). Updates add them turned off
- Codex: Business plans show the monthly per-user limit an admin set
- Settings open in a wider panel, in groups like Windows Settings: Usage, Providers, Notifications, Taskbar & desktop, Appearance and App in a list on the left, the chosen group's cards beside it. The panel itself gets wider by dragging its left or right edge, and the provider bar can sit on the right
- A proxy for provider, status page and update requests (http, https or socks5)
- Hide from screen sharing: the panel and the desktop widgets stay out of screen shares, recordings and screenshots
- Themes: Glass blurs the desktop behind the panel (Windows 11), and a Halloween theme
- Reset all settings, keeping your providers, accounts and project budgets
- What's new: once after an update, the panel shows the release notes and a short video (can be turned off)
Bug Fixes
- The response log hides account display names and subscription ids too
